newsitem.title: POLAND: SOCCER-WOJCIK PICKED AS NEW POLISH TEAM COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WOJCIK PICKED AS NEW POLISH TEAM COACH.

text.p: Former Olympic coach Janusz Wojcik will be the new Polish national team coach, the Polish Soccer Association (PZPN) said on Wednesday.
Wojcik, 44, takes over from Antoni Piechniczek who quit last month following a 2-0 home defeat to England which ended Poland's hopes of qualifying for the 1998 World Cup.
Wojcik first won national fame by guiding Poland to a silver medal at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics and has spent the last three years coaching in the United Arab Emirates.

"Working with the national team has long been my dream and right now with (new assistant coach Edward) Lorens we are discussing our goals for the first half-year," PAP news agency quoted Wojcik as saying.
Following Piechniczek's resignation an interim coach led Poland to 4-1 victory over Georgia in their World Cup qualifier with a drastically reshaped squad.

Critics hope Wojcik will end the unpopular policies of the former coach, who often snubbed Polish players with foreign clubs because they could not meet his training demands and constantly changed line-ups.
"Simply, the national side will consist of Poland's best players," Wojcik was quoted as saying.
In 1993 Wojcik guided Legia Warsaw to the national club championship but the title was later taken away from them because of alleged game-rigging.
